title: The Leeward Monsoon
premise: Odile Dravenmoor, a salvage diver haunted by the sister she lost to a flooded mine, works the wreck of the Vesperine — a ship of the drowned nation of Calveth that the navy quietly forbids anyone to name. When the river surrenders a chest bearing Calveth's seal, containing her sister's handwriting among state papers, Odile assembles a ragtag crew of drifters who become the family neither of them had. Racing a licensed salvage fleet across six tides, they discover the Vesperine carried not treasure but a census of the drowned — proof that Calveth's sinking was engineered, and that Odile's own family helped do it. In the end, Odile chooses to give the archive to the descendants of the drowned rather than sell it, scuttling the fleet's claim and finally letting herself stop moving.
about_author: Ivo Brightwater is the pen name of a former river pilot who spent a decade working salvage crews on inland waterways before turning to fiction. They write adventure stories about people who belong to water more than land.

chapters.title: The Bottom of the Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Diving the Vesperine's outer hull at dawn, Odile catalogs what the navy won't discuss and pockets a brass fitting stamped with Calveth's seal. The emotional beat is restless competence masking grief — every dive is a way of not stopping long enough to remember.

chapters.title: What the River Gives Up
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A spring flood shifts the riverbed and delivers a sealed chest onto the shallows near Odile's camp. Inside: Calveth state papers and a letter in her dead sister Wren's handwriting. Shock and vertigo; the past has physically surfaced.

chapters.title: Six Tides
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A harbor official tips Odile off that the Meridian Salvage Fleet holds a wreck claim expiring in six tides — after which anything raised belongs to whoever holds it. Odile decides to beat them there. The beat is resolve born of desperation.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile recruits three drifters: Tam, a disgraced naval cartographer; Sefa, a deaf rigging master; and Bo, a teenage runaway who can read old Calvethi script. First sparks of reluctant trust; found family begins assembling itself.

chapters.title: The Navy Won't Discuss It
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Tam decodes the chest's papers and finds the Vesperine listed as 'expunged' — sunk deliberately, its manifest erased. A navy patrol boat shadows them. Paranoia sets in; the crew realizes this is bigger than salvage.

chapters.title: Downstream, Running Dark
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Running without lights through a lock system at night, Sefa reads the water by feel and vibration while the patrol boat hunts them. A tense, sensory chapter whose beat is the crew learning to trust each other's hands.

chapters.title: The Drowned Census
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Bo translates a fragment: the Vesperine carried a census naming every citizen lost when Calveth was flooded — and an order signed with a surname Odile recognizes as her own family's. Guilt lands like cold water.

chapters.title: Wren's Hand
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reading Wren's letter fully for the first time, Odile learns Wren survived the initial sinking and died later, investigating. Grief curdles into purpose: finish what Wren started. The emotional core of the book.

chapters.title: Tide Two: The Fleet
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The Meridian Fleet appears on the horizon, led by Captain Ilse Varn, who offers Odile a partnership that is really a bribe. Odile refuses. Beat: drawing a line, and making an enemy.

chapters.title: The Leeward Passage
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. To gain a tide, the crew takes the leeward passage through shoals no chart survives. Sefa navigates by memory of a route her grandmother once ran. Triumph and inheritance braided together — the theme made literal.

chapters.title: Bo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Bo secretly contacts Meridian, offering to translate the census in exchange for protection, believing Odile will sell it anyway. Betrayal motivated by fear of being abandoned first. Heartbreak beat.

chapters.title: Tide Three: The Outer Wreck
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Deep dive into the Vesperine's hold. Odile finds the census vault but triggers a collapse that traps Bo above. Rescue succeeds, but Bo's secret deal surfaces. Anger, then a hard-won forgiveness — family means staying anyway.

chapters.title: Varn's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. Captured briefly by Meridian, Tam sees Varn's own records: the navy pays her to keep Calveth buried. She releases him with a warning. Beat: understanding the enemy's machinery, and its rot.

chapters.title: Tide Four: The Vault Room
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The crew breaches the census vault and finds it intact — thousands of names, plus engineering orders proving the flood was ordered. Awe and horror; history becomes personal responsibility.

chapters.title: Descendants of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. Bo finds their own family name in the census — they are Calvethi descent, which is why they could read the script. Identity crystallizes; the runaway becomes an heir.

chapters.title: Tide Five: The Trap
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Varn blockades the only exit channel. Sefa proposes a desperate plan: use the wreck itself as leverage, threatening to open the hull and scatter the archive beyond any claim. Stakes peak; unity solidifies.

chapters.title: Odile's Name
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile confronts the truth that her grandfather signed the flooding order, and confesses it to the crew, offering to walk away. Instead they stay. The found-family theme reaches its full weight: chosen over blood.

chapters.title: Tide Six: The Standoff
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Climax. At slack water, with Varn boarding, Odile opens the sea cocks and forces the choice: sink the evidence or let the world read it. Varn's own crew, many descended from the drowned, mutiny and stand down.

chapters.title: What Rises
chapters.summary: Tam's POV. The census is raised publicly; the navy's cover fractures under the weight of names. Tam testifies with his old charts as evidence. Vindication beat — quiet, procedural, earned.

chapters.title: The Weight of Names
chapters.summary: Bo's POV. A memorial reading of the census on the shore where Calveth stood. Bo speaks their family's names aloud. Grief transformed into belonging; the drowned are given back their story.

chapters.title: Anchored
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. The crew refits the salvaged Vesperine's bell into a small boat and decides not to disband. Sefa, who never stayed anywhere, chooses a home port. Warmth after storm; the family holds.

chapters.title: Where the Water Stops Moving
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Epilogue. Odile dives one last time — not for salvage, but to leave Wren's letter in the wreck, then surfaces and stays ashore. Final beat: stillness chosen freely, the thing she feared most becoming peace.
